summary: Both sides are the same full-brightness rainbow that scrolls smoothly along the strip at a slider-controlled speed, and they agree pixel-for-pixel in structure, direction and speed at every dialed slider value; the only real difference is the untouched default, where the original runs at full speed and the port runs at exactly one quarter of it.
observations: Control surface matches exactly: both sides expose one control, name 'sliderSpeed', kind 'slider', label 'Speed'.

Structure is identical on both sides: exactly one full HSV rainbow spanning the strip, saturation and value railed (meanBrightness pinned at 127 with min=max=127 on both, meanR=meanG=meanB=127), no dark pixels or gaps. --dump at t=0 shows hue rising a uniform 1/60 cycle per pixel on both (orig 0.049->0.983 across 60 px, port 0.012->0.996).
Both are resolution-independent: re-rendered at --pixels 12 each side still draws exactly one rainbow across the strip (hue step 1/12 per pixel on both), so neither rasterizes at a fixed 60-px scale.

Motion is the same on both: a smooth, continuous, constant-velocity translation toward pixel 0 (the whole-strip hue offset increases monotonically with time on both sides), no jitter, no bounce, no reset, no modes.

Single regime only. A 60 s / 5 fps survey and a 240 s / 2 fps survey both show unbroken uniform diagonal banding on each side with no regime boundary, and a late window (--skip 40) renders the same as t=0. brightnessTrend 'steady' and zeroMotionFrames=1 (the unavoidable first frame) on both sides in every run; neither side decays, freezes or saturates.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULT SPEED DIVERGES 4x. Measured as whole-strip hue-offset rate over a 19 s baseline: original 0.9918 cycles/s (one full traversal of the strip per second), port 0.2441 cycles/s. Whole-window motion stat: orig 25, port 6 at 20 fps. The port's untouched rate is exactly the rate BOTH sides produce at sliderSpeed=0.5, and the original's untouched rate is the rate both sides produce at sliderSpeed=1 - i.e. the port's speed variable starts at half-slider where the original's starts at full.

Dialed, the speed mapping is the same quadratic curve on both sides. Long-baseline rates (cycles/s), orig vs port: sliderSpeed=0 -> 0.0000 / 0.0000; 0.25 -> 0.06102 / 0.06102; 0.5 -> 0.24415 / 0.24415; 0.75 -> 0.54931 / 0.54931. All agree to five decimals, and the whole-window motion stats are identical integers (0/0, 2/2, 6/6, 14/14).

At the very top of the slider only, the original is marginally faster: sliderSpeed=1 gives orig 0.9918 cycles/s vs port 0.9765 (1.6% slower). The port sits exactly on the fitted curve rate = 0.9766 * v^2; the original is 1.6% above it at v=1 alone. Visually indistinguishable (a full cycle of phase drift takes ~65 s) but it is a real, repeatable difference.

Both sides are frame-rate independent: rendering each at --fps 10 / 20 / 40 gives per-second hue rates of 0.9913 / 0.9935 / 0.9956 (orig) and 0.2440 / 0.2440 / 0.2440 (port), and the motion stat halves as fps doubles on both. Neither side is frame-stepped.
No randomness: seed 1234 renders byte-identical stats to seed 1 on both sides.
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both); no compile or runtime errors on either side in any run.

No smoothing/ramp transient is visible on either side when a control is applied at init: at sliderSpeed=0 both sides post motion 0 on every one of 240 captured frames from frame 0 (no decay from a faster default), and at sliderSpeed=1 both jump to motion 25 on frame 1 and hold. Whatever 'smooth' means in this pattern, it is not observable through the harness's set-at-init control path, and the two sides behave identically there.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Sets scroll speed on a quadratic curve from dead stop to ~1 full strip traversal per second: 0 -> frozen rainbow, 0.25 -> 0.061 cyc/s, 0.5 -> 0.244 cyc/s, 0.75 -> 0.549 cyc/s, 1 -> 0.992 cyc/s. Direction, colour and structure are unaffected; only speed changes. Untouched, the original runs as if the slider were at 1.
dials.portEffect: Identical curve and identical rates at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 (agreeing to five decimal places); at 1 it reaches 0.9765 cyc/s, 1.6% slower than the original. Also affects only speed. Untouched, the port runs as if the slider were at 0.5, i.e. a quarter of the original's default speed.

feedback: Fix the untouched default speed: with no control applied the original scrolls the rainbow at ~0.992 cycles/s (one full pass along the strip per second, motion stat 25 at 20 fps) while the port scrolls at ~0.244 cycles/s (motion 6). The port's initial speed state corresponds to sliderSpeed=0.5; it should correspond to sliderSpeed=1 (top of the slider). Everything downstream of that value is already correct, so this is purely the value the speed state holds before any control is set.

Optional nitpick, only if it is free: at sliderSpeed=1 the port runs 1.6% slower than the original (0.9765 vs 0.9918 cycles/s). The port's rate follows rate = 0.9766 * v^2 exactly across the whole slider range; the original follows the same curve at 0.25/0.5/0.75 but sits 1.6% above it at v=1. Do not chase this at the cost of the mid-range agreement, which is currently exact.

Nothing else needs changing: spatial layout (one rainbow across the strip, resolution-independent), colour (railed saturation and value, meanBrightness 127 flat), scroll direction, smoothness, frame-rate independence, steady state over 240 s, and the control surface (sliderSpeed / slider / 'Speed') all already match the original exactly.
